title: fix(types): serialize deferred pydantic schema builds across threads
body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- First concurrent requests to a fresh worker can answer 400 `'CredentialLiteLLMParams' object has no attribute 'use_litellm_proxy'`
- Pydantic's deferred schema build is not thread-safe, so a second thread's rebuild deleted the first thread's freshly built validator
- Regression from #44720, which turned deferred builds on for every LiteLLM model

How it solves it:

- `LiteLLMBaseModel.model_rebuild` now runs under one process-wide re-entrant lock
- A thread that arrives mid-build waits for the finished validator instead of rebuilding over it
- Regression test fires 16 threads at a fresh deferred subclass 100 times and expects only that subclass back

## User Flow

Before: a team restarts their two-worker gateway and the first burst of concurrent chat completions gets one or two 400s that name a LiteLLM internal, with no fallback tried

1. They start the gateway with two workers and wait for `GET https://litellm-domain/health/readiness` to return 200
2. Their app, on the OpenAI SDK, sends 8 concurrent `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [...]}` and a virtual key
3. 6 or 7 come back 200 with a `chatcmpl-...` id and the model's reply
4. 1 or 2 come back 400 `Invalid request format: litellm.BadRequestError: GetLLMProvider Exception - 'CredentialLiteLLMParams' object has no attribute 'use_litellm_proxy' ... No fallback was attempted.` for a body identical to the ones that succeeded
5. The same request a moment later returns 200, but the app already treated the 400 as a caller error and surfaced it to its user

After: the same restart and burst answers every request 200

1. They start the gateway with two workers and wait for `GET https://litellm-domain/health/readiness` to return 200
2. Their app, on the OpenAI SDK, sends 8 concurrent `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [...]}` and a virtual key
3. All 8 come back 200 with a `chatcmpl-...` id and the model's reply
4. No 400 appears in that burst or any later one

## Affected release

regression in v1.106.0-dev.1 (#44720 is not on rc/1.105.0, so no released rc or stable carries it)

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup: an 8 vCPU Linux box (Python 3.12.3, pydantic 2.13.4, like CI's cimg/python:3.12 image), the CircleCI `integration-extensions` job's environment rebuilt from `.circleci/scripts/run_integration.sh` (own Postgres database, own redis, the upstream stub, a one-worker shared proxy with `num_retries: 0`), and `tests/integration/observability/test_s3_v2_partition_granularity.py` run the way the job runs it, one pytest process per run through `tests/integration/run.py extensions` with `-p no:cacheprovider`. Every test in that file boots its own two-worker proxy and fires a burst of concurrent chat completions through the OpenAI SDK at it, which is the flow CircleCI pipeline 90977 failed on. The two tests that fail in every run on both sides (`test_s3_v2_audit_logs_follow_the_audit_params_granularity_not_the_request_logs` and `test_s3_v2_hour_postgres_outage_mid_mixed_burst_lands_every_id_exactly_once_and_recovers`) are artifacts of this box and pass in CI, so they are not counted on either side

### Before (17a982d6df, the merge base; the rig runs used a worktree at d1cfe17518, the commit pipeline 90977 ran, whose base.py has the same race)

#### CI-shaped runs of the s3_v2 granularity file

1. `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do run_test.sh results/base/run$i tests/integration/observability/test_s3_v2_partition_granularity.py; done`
2. Observed: 2 of 5 runs failed one test with the 400 below (the run's other failures are the two box artifacts named above)

   | run | result | 400s with the CI message | test that hit it |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | 1 | 3 failed, 31 passed | 1 | test_s3_v2_hour_granularity_files_every_surface_under_its_hour_folder |
   | 2 | 2 failed, 32 passed | 0 | none |
   | 3 | 3 failed, 31 passed | 1 | test_s3_v2_hour_slow_sink_batches_never_duplicate_an_upload |
   | 4 | 2 failed, 32 passed | 0 | none |
   | 5 | 2 failed, 32 passed | 0 | none |
3. The failing request's 400 body, as the OpenAI SDK raised it:

```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Invalid request format: litellm.BadRequestError: GetLLMProvider Exception - 'CredentialLiteLLMParams' object has no attribute 'use_litellm_proxy'\n\noriginal model: openai/gpt-4o-mini\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'integration-a338118e09db42a79ca100dd26b34604' failed with the error above. No fallback was attempted.", 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': None, 'code': '400'}}
```

#### Regression test

1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/types/llms/test_types_llms_base.py::test_concurrent_first_use_of_a_deferred_subclass_always_builds_that_subclass`
2. Fails in every trial within the first 20 rounds: `AssertionError: round 1`, `round 20`, `round 15`, with `AttributeError: type object 'Child1' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'` among the outcomes (the other shape the race produces is a `Parent1` instance where a `Child1` was asked for)

### After (c04516e0e1)

#### CI-shaped runs of the s3_v2 granularity file

1. `for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do run_test.sh results/after/run$i tests/integration/observability/test_s3_v2_partition_granularity.py; done`
2. The 8 runs at the tip are in progress on the same box; this case is filled in from their logs when they finish

#### Regression test

1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/types/llms/test_types_llms_base.py::test_concurrent_first_use_of_a_deferred_subclass_always_builds_that_subclass`
2. `1 passed in 1.55s`, `1 passed in 1.53s`; the whole file: `10 passed in 29.05s`

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- The lock is process-wide, so two threads building unrelated models wait on each other once, at first use
- The regression test is statistical: it reproduced in every one of 8 unfixed trials, always within 20 of its 100 rounds
- The rebuild's thread-safety is pydantic's gap (its own comment says `model_rebuild()` isn't thread-safe); the lock stays until pydantic closes it

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches all LiteLLM Pydantic models at first-use rebuild under a global lock; low behavioral change but affects hot-path concurrency on worker cold start.
> 
> **Overview**
> Serializes **deferred Pydantic schema builds** on `LiteLLMBaseModel` by wrapping `model_rebuild()` in a process-wide re-entrant lock (`threading.RLock`), so concurrent first-use validation on a fresh worker no longer races and corrupts validators (e.g. intermittent 400s naming missing attributes on internal credential types).
> 
> Adds a **stress regression test** that runs 16 threads against freshly created deferred subclasses for 100 rounds and asserts every validation returns the expected model class.
>
